title: 3.8.24 Saving and Loading Data
description: Eight multiple-choice questions on JSON.stringify, JSON.parse, what does not survive a round trip, parse failures, saving by key with localStorage, and the browser sandbox. Checked instantly.

questions.question: The program does '' + student, where student is an object, and prints the result. What comes out?
options: The full object, printed as JSON
[object Object]
An error
null
questions.explanation: Turning an object into text without JSON.stringify gives the label [object Object], which throws away every property. There is no way to restore the data from it.

questions.question: What does JSON.stringify([1, 2, 3]) produce, and what type is the result?
options: The array [1, 2, 3], type object
The number 6, type number
[object Object], type string
The string "[1,2,3]", type string
questions.explanation: Arrays convert just like objects, and the result is always a string. The spaces are dropped in the compact form.

questions.question: What does the third argument in JSON.stringify(student, null, 2) control?
options: How many spaces to indent by, making the output readable for a person
The maximum number of properties to include
Whether strings use single or double quotes
The output's position in the console
questions.explanation: The null is a filter you almost never need; the 2 is the indent width. Use it for output a human reads, and leave it off for the smaller compact form a program reads.

questions.question: An object has a count property and a describe method. What does JSON.stringify produce for it?
options: {"count":5,"describe":"function"}
Only {"count":5} — the method is dropped silently
An error, because objects with methods cannot be serialized
{"count":5,"describe":null}
questions.explanation: JSON has no way to represent a function, so methods are dropped, along with undefined values. That is JSON storing data rather than behaviour, not a bug.

questions.question: After const v = JSON.parse('{"n": 5}'); what is v.n + 1, and why?
options: "51", because parsing returns strings
NaN, because v.n is not a number
6, because parse restores the number as a real number
undefined, because n was not preserved
questions.explanation: JSON.parse rebuilds objects, arrays and numbers as real values, so v.n is the number 5 and + adds. It would only join strings if the JSON had contained "n": "5".

questions.question: Why does JSON.parse need a try...catch when JSON.stringify does not?
options: JSON.parse is slower than stringify
stringify starts from a valid JavaScript value; parse starts from text that may be malformed
stringify returns null on failure instead of throwing
JSON.parse only fails on very large objects
questions.explanation: You always hand stringify a real value, so there is nothing to be invalid. You hand parse text — often from storage, a file, or a network — and text can be anything, so a bad string throws a SyntaxError.

questions.question: What does localStorage.getItem("neverSaved") return on a first run?
options: undefined
An empty string
null
questions.explanation: A key that was never saved gives null, not undefined. That is why a load function tests for null before parsing: JSON.parse(null) quietly returns null rather than throwing, so the missing-data case would slip through unnoticed.

questions.question: After localStorage.setItem("count", 5), what does localStorage.getItem("count") + 1 give?
options: "51", because storage holds strings so the + joins text
null
NaN
questions.explanation: Storage holds strings only, so the 5 became "5" on the way in and + joined it to "1". Wrap the read in Number(...) to add numerically.

questions.question: Why can JavaScript running in a web page not open a file on your computer by name?
options: JavaScript is too slow to read files
Files must be converted to JSON before they can be read
Any page could then read your files just because you visited it
The browser has not implemented open() yet
questions.explanation: A page runs code you did not write, so the browser gives it no filesystem access at all. Reading a local file requires the user to choose it, or the page to offer a download the user saves.
